target_customer: College and high school students (and later schools and state agencies) paying for exam review sessions and video courses
problem: Students in large gateway university courses needed affordable exam review and tutoring; the founder began by running paid review sessions for a UF managerial accounting exam.
business_model: B2C paid review sessions and video course subscriptions, later B2B/B2G curriculum licensing (Algebra Nation, Math Nation)

founders.name: Ethan Fieldman
previous_startups: Ethan the Tutor (informal tutoring business that preceded Study Edge)
founders.background_notes: As a UF sophomore he handed out flyers for a managerial accounting review session that grew to more than 400 paying students, per a local profile.

technical_complexity.rationale: Core offer was live review sessions and recorded video; the work was content production and local operations rather than novel engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Local campus reputation and tutor content helped, but a rival tutoring firm (TutoringZone, from which the founding tutors left in 2011) offered the same service and tutors could leave.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought it. A Carlyle-backed Accelerate Learning acquired it in October 2021.

market_need_then: Large lecture courses at the University of Florida created demand for paid exam review; the founder's early sessions drew over 400 paying students.

branding.community_and_virality: Student word of mouth and campus presence at UF, Florida State and Georgia are described in local press; no merch or fan communities found.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong local campus recognition at UF per local coverage, but no source shows brand press, mascot or national recognition.

outcome_analysis: Study Edge grew from a founder-run exam review at the University of Florida into a multi-campus tutoring and video course business, and was acquired in October 2021 by Accelerate Learning, a company backed by Carlyle (the YC page says acquired by Carlyle). It looks capital efficient: no verified institutional round was found, only conflicting aggregator figures, so the outcome was reached with little disclosed outside money. Deal terms were not disclosed.
notes: Company website fetch returned only navigation (courses, pricing, help), no history. Business Wire release returned 403, so the acquirer detail comes from search results listing the release and MergerLinks. PPP), PitchBook $150K, one site a $100K 2012 seed; none confirmed by a primary source, so none is recorded as a round. CB Insights names a different founder (Ashley Fieldman), which conflicts with the YC page. Local press says nine TutoringZone tutors left in June 2011 to start Study Edge; I could not map that to a specific article URL, so no competitor entry is recorded. Seed (Seedtable, no amount) and two PPP-related debt rounds (ZoomInfo) added, each from a single database; CB Insights $270K, PitchBook $150K and a $100K seed claim conflict and were not summed.
